A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the strainmeters are the most powerful tools to observe the lowest-frequency Earth normal modes.
the strainmeter data provide a unique tool to study the Earth’s lowest-frequency modes and to test Earth models.

strainmeter data are very promising to obtain the fundamental mode of the Earth, and to improve the determination of the Earth’s rotation parameters and the Earth’s free oscillations in the frequency band between 1 and 2 mHz.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the invar strainmeters are a very powerful tool to study the lowest-frequency normal mode of the Earth.

invar-wire vertical strainmeters are excellent tools to study low-frequency Earth modes and can provide a complementary data set to the vertical accelerometers for the study of the lowest-frequency normal mode spectra.
